newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Levy blasts Israeli general's comments on Syria.
newsitem.headline: Levy blasts Israeli general's comments on Syria.

text.p: Foreign Minister David Levy blasted on Wednesday an Israeli general's warning that Syria would get "clobbered" if it started a war, saying such declarations only stoked tensions with Damascus.

Levy, who is not part of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's inner circle, also repeated his long-standing position that peace with Syria was impossible without territorial compromise on the Israeli-held Golan Heights.
"I can tell you with full confidence the Israeli army is prepared for war," Deputy Chief of Staff Matan Vilnai said in a speech late on Monday.
"(Syrian President Hafez al-) Assad has no illusions as to what will happen to him if he starts to fight us...He knows he will get clobbered," Major-General Vilnai said.
Asked about the statement, Levy told Israeli Army Radio: "There is no need for these declarations -- Israel's strength is known."
He said such remarks were likely to draw Syrian accusations that Israel was preparing to attack.
"We are working towards a return to peace negotiations (with Syria)," Levy said. "An escalation of declarations is unnecessary."
War jitters in Israel rose in recent months after Syrian forces in Lebanon redeployed within striking distance of a key Israeli position on the Golan.
Netanyahu has said the tensions have dropped following "calming messages" sent through international mediators.
Levy reiterated his long-standing position that peace with Syria would entail a return of parts of the Golan.
Levy reiterated his belief that Israel would have to meet Syria "halfway" on the Golan, although he insisted he was not drawing any exact withdrawal lines.
"I repeat: Whoever thinks it is possible to attain peace without any movement (on the ground) or compromise -- I support him but I just want to know how he is going to achieve this," he said.
Any renewed talks with Syria -- negotiations have been frozen since March -- would be doomed to "explode" if Israel continued to insist it would maintain control of all of the Golan, Levy said.

Netanyahu already distanced himself from Levy's support for "cosmetic adjustments" on the Golan when the foreign minister spelled out his stance after Israel's right-wing government came to power last June.
The government's policy guidelines say: "Retaining Israeli sovereignty over the Golan will be the basis for an arrangement with Syria."
Israel captured the Golan Heights from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war. Syria insists on the return of all the strategic plateau.
